thesis: Joby Aviation is the best-capitalized pure-play in electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) air taxis, targeting commercial passenger service as it works through the final stages of FAA type certification. A ~$2.5B cash and short-term investment war chest (Q1 2026), a deepening Toyota manufacturing joint venture, a finalized Virgin Atlantic UK partnership, the Blade passenger-mobility acquisition, and a planned Dubai launch give it a credible path to first revenue that most competitors lack. The counterweight is a pre-commercial business burning ~$500M a year, a binary dependence on FAA certification timing, and heavy dilution risk — the stock trades near its 52-week low of $6.89 despite the news flow.

drivers: FAA type certification achieved on schedule, unlocking U.S. commercial passenger service
Dubai commercial launch with RTA proves the operating model and generates first meaningful air-taxi revenue
Toyota manufacturing joint venture scales S4 production toward hundreds of aircraft per year
Virgin Atlantic UK and Japan/Korea partnerships open multiple international markets ahead of peers

base_case.assumptions: Certification and commercial launch slip modestly but stay on track into 2027; Dubai and early U.S. routes ramp slowly; Blade contributes near-term revenue; the ~$2.5B balance sheet funds the path to commercialization with periodic, manageable dilution; the stock re-rates toward the ~$11 analyst consensus target

risks: FAA certification delays push commercial service out multiple years and erode investor patience
Persistent ~$500M annual cash burn forces large, dilutive equity raises
Manufacturing scale-up or supply-chain issues delay production ramp
eVTOL sector sentiment sours and unit economics or demand disappoint at launch

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings — cash burn, certification progress, and Toyota JV / Blade updates
FAA type certification flight-testing milestones (final stages)
Dubai commercial air-taxi launch with the Road and Transport Authority
Toyota manufacturing joint venture production scale-up of the S4 aircraft
Targeted U.S. commercial passenger service launch pending certification

key_risks: Binary FAA type-certification risk — timing is uncertain and commercial revenue is gated on it
Pre-commercial with ~$500M annual cash burn and a multi-year path to profitability; future raises would be dilutive
Roughly 984M shares outstanding and a history of equity issuance create ongoing dilution overhang
Manufacturing and supply-chain execution risk as the Toyota JV scales S4 production
eVTOL demand, unit economics, and infrastructure (vertiports, charging) remain unproven at commercial scale
High volatility (beta ~2.7) and sector-sentiment swings; stock trades near its 52-week low
